claims.text: Single-phase formation is governed by the interplay of rapid thermal kinetics and surface diffusion.
Rapid heating and cooling hinder sufficient atomic mixing.
Rapid heating and cooling hinder surface equilibration.
An intermediate-temperature thermal hold or moderated cooling rate enhances surface-mediated atomic diffusion.
Enhanced diffusion can overcome local composition fluctuations and kinetic barriers.
Overcoming local composition fluctuations favors a uniform single-phase solid solution.
Rapidly heated and cooled noble-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles often exhibit phase separation.
Rapidly heated and cooled noble-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles often exhibit elemental segregation.
Rapidly heated and cooled noble-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles often exhibit uncontrolled particle morphology.
The controlled intervention is an intermediate-temperature thermal hold or a moderated cooling rate.
Surface and interfacial energy differences mediate atomic mobility and mixing.
Particle-surface diffusion kinetics govern phase nucleation and growth.
Rapid quenching without a sufficient hold traps atoms in nonequilibrium positions.
Nonequilibrium atomic trapping leads to phase separation and elemental segregation.
The controlled thermal intervention will increase the predominance of the single-phase solid solution relative to the rapid-heating and rapid-cooling baseline.
The controlled thermal intervention will reduce elemental segregation relative to the baseline.
The controlled thermal intervention will improve particle-morphology control relative to the baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies to nanoparticles containing more than five noble-metal components when atomic-size mismatch and mixing enthalpy permit a high-entropy configuration.
The thermal hold must be above the minimum temperature required for surface diffusion, below decomposition onset, and under non-oxidizing conditions.
The relative importance of surface and bulk diffusion may vary with elemental combination and particle size.
